alice_support: FYI — ACCT-832 (reported via email) says a critical chat flow started returning inconsistent answers after last night's rollout. They run the same conversation twice and get different structured outputs mid-session. They attached request IDs and a short repro.

alice_support: Customer repro (pasted):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" \ 
  -d '{"model":"gptx-stable:alias", "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Summarize the policy in 3 bullets"}]}'
# Request IDs: r-0a12b3, r-0a12b4
# First call returns bullet list (good). Second call in same session returns a paragraph (regression).
```

alice_support: Visible in their headers: `x-route=eu-west-1|primary` for the first, then `x-route=eu-west-1|fallback` for the second. They suspect routing->fallback is swapping a variant.

chris_oncall: Thanks — can you paste exact `x-request-id` headers and the `model` field they sent? Is the customer using a pinned model alias or a dynamic alias?

alice_support: Provided in the ticket: `req-20260314-9f2`, `req-20260314-9f3`. They call `model: gptx-stable:alias` (alias points to v1 and v1-q8 as fallback).

maya_ml: tagging in — this smells like variant mismatch across rollouts. We had the canary for `gptx-stable` flip a fallback policy that routes to `v1-q8` (quantized) under latency or capacity pressure. Quantized variant may change verbosity/formatting.

violet_prod: How large was the canary? I thought rollout was 10% traffic -> 50% at 02:00 UTC. Deploy bot should confirm.

deploy-bot: Deployment event: `rollout/gptx-stable@2026-03-14T01:20Z` -> canary 10% -> 50% at 02:15Z. Autoscale policy `latency-fallback=true` enabled.

rohit_sre: Repro steps for us: force fallback by setting `X-RW-Routing-Hint: fallback` in header or reduce pool capacity. Also we can call the variant explicitly: `model: gptx-stable@v1-q8` vs `gptx-stable@v1`.

chris_oncall: I'll grab logs for those request IDs. If both requests hit different variants, that's our cause. Also need to check session affinity: are we preserving the same model/route within a session?

maya_ml: Note — we intentionally don't guarantee identical outputs across quantization variants. But session-level consistency is expected when alias resolution happens at request time. If routing changes mid-session due to policy, that creates user-visible regressions.

alice_support: Customer is pretty unhappy — they use chat for contract clause extraction and rely on consistent structured replies. They flagged this as severity P1. Asking for workaround asap.

violet_prod: Workaround options: 1) Ask customer to pin to `gptx-stable@v1` (explicit version) — immediate. 2) Disable latency-fallback for their tenant (assigned to Dedicated/Private only?). We can apply a routing override for the customer account (support can request tenant-level route policy).

rohit_sre: I can flip a routing override for ACCT-832 to `prefer: primary` for 24h. Need account id + approval.

chris_oncall: Logs: both request IDs present. r-0a12b3 -> backend `node-pla-17` -> variant `v1` -> tokens 48ms/core. r-0a12b4 -> backend `node-pla-09` -> variant `v1-q8` -> tokens 26ms/core. So confirmed different variants.

maya_ml: That explains formatting differences. We should: (A) roll back the `latency-fallback=true` toggle for the alias until we have quantized parity tests, (B) add regression alerting that fires when an alias resolves to >1 variant for a single customer session in <30s.

violet_prod: I'll open an incident and tag QA to run a focused eval comparing `v1` vs `v1-q8` on the customer's prompt set. Also product decision: do we consider variant-parity a requirement for aliasing?

alice_support: For immediate customer reply: propose pin to explicit version + offer routing override while we investigate. Customer prefers patch faster than diagnostic deep-dive.

chris_oncall: Assigning owners: rohit_sre = apply tenant override; maya_ml = run parity eval + confirm behavioral diffs; violet_prod = incident + rollout governance; alice_support = customer comms.

deploy-bot: Support ticket ACCT-832 updated: `routing_override_requested` by alice_support at 2026-03-14T09:45Z.

rohit_sre: I'll prepare the override and post back the change ID.

alice_support: Thanks — please also include the workaround text I can send to the customer: short steps to pin model or request override.

maya_ml: Long-term: we should add a deterministic resolution layer for session affinity when alias points to multiple variants. If latency fallback triggers, route but also signal the client that variant changed (header `x-model-variant-changed: true`) so SDKs can surface a warning.

chris_oncall: Noted. For now, customer pinned and override created (change-id r-ov-447). Customer confirmed pinned test passes and behavior consistent. Closing P1 for now; will keep incident open for root cause until parity tests done. :white_check_mark:

alice_support: Great — closing loop with customer now. Thanks all.
